## Everything stays in step

This release is about places where two parts of Resesh kept their own copy of the same thing and drifted apart. Most of these fixes are small on their own, but together they remove a lot of "it only updates after a restart".

- Every window now follows the saved sessions, settings, highlight rules, workspaces, identities and SSH keys. An edit, an import or a restored backup shows everywhere at once, and a tab no longer saves an old copy of its session back over a newer one.
- A tab follows the connection it actually made. Turning persistence on or off for a session no longer lets a tab end another tab's persistent shell, and the file pane, Manage Remote Sessions and File Explorer use the login and route the terminal connected with rather than the edited session.
- The tab's right-click menu and the Session menu offer the same actions under the same rules.
- "Update from current layout" saves the workspace it names, not whichever one is showing, and "Add to current layout" no longer opens a workspace's connections twice.
- Dragged pane sizes stay put when another pane splits or closes.

## Connections

- IPv6 hosts work in quick connect, telnet, ProxyJump and imports: `ssh ::1` and `ssh [::1]:2222` connect where they should, and a host saved with brackets by an older build is recognised as the same known host.
- A session with no port set connects to the protocol's default port instead of port 0.
- A jump host that drops without closing is noticed, and the tabs that run through it end instead of sitting connected.
- File Explorer (SSHFS) mounts follow the SSH algorithm settings, offer RSA SHA-2 host keys to modern servers, and find a session's registered key before the tab connects.
- Proxy settings that are incomplete are treated as unused everywhere, not only when dialling.

## Files

- A dropped connection no longer leaves a truncated download that looks complete, and a failed upload no longer destroys the file it was replacing. Uploads write through symlinks instead of replacing them, and leave files owned by another user with their owner.
- Download and Open opens the file that was written, even when it had to pick a new name.
- Relative paths typed into the remote file pane resolve from the folder shown, and names such as `..`, `CON` or `name.` are refused up front.

## Backups and imports

- Restoring a backup brings back everything: workspaces and icons in the right data folder, proxy passwords, recent sessions, folder logins and highlight rules, and the restored SSH algorithm settings take effect without a restart.
- Backups and imports are checked completely before anything is written, so a bad file no longer stops part way. A failed SecureCRT, PuTTY or OpenSSH import undoes the identities and keys it created.
- A telnet line is no longer skipped as a duplicate of an SSH session with the same address.
- Folders that hold an identity no longer vanish when their last session moves out.

## Terminal and history

- Inserting a multi-line command from history keeps history open until you accept it, and cancelling goes back to history.
- Splitting, zooming or closing a tab from the palette or session filter moves focus to the terminal, while tabs opening or closing in the background no longer pull focus out of the filter.
- The commands panel and ruler card use the font the terminal draws, and follow font changes.
- Highlight rules with a colour the terminal can't read are marked as not applied in the editor.
- The working folder shown in the subtitle, history and file pane comes from the newest report, so a stale one no longer wins.
- The recording player shows hours past 24, and history durations no longer read "60 s" or "1000 ms".

## Look and feel

- Icons stay sharp on every monitor, including after the window that opened first closes.
- Focus borders, filter matches and status colours follow the window's current theme, and status dots and badges have High Contrast colours.
- The sessions pane no longer slides when Windows animations are off.
- Renaming a tab or key to the same name leaves it alone, so the tab keeps following the session's name.

Choose the x64 download for Intel or AMD PCs. Choose ARM64 only for Windows on ARM devices.
